result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A has the tighter shared system. A single content/wide/full grid and one spacing token serve both docs and marketing, there are only three breakpoints, and the shell stops growing at a clear 1440px cap. It has small flaws: the 4/8-column scheme in its table is never implemented, and 52ch appears as a literal number even though a matching token exists. Answer B handles code and tables more thoroughly, including bleeding them to the screen edge on phones, but its CSS is messier: a duplicated `.pricing` block with a `composes` line that only works in CSS modules, repeated magic numbers (34rem, 4rem, 28rem), a fourth breakpoint, and root-font scaling that keeps the page growing on very large monitors. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B uses one content/wide/full grid that serves both articles and marketing. Code and tables break out to the wide track and scroll, and it gets by with three breakpoints and a clear 1440px cap. A is thorough, with good phone bleed and min-width fixes, but its CSS has an invalid `composes` line, defines the pricing grid twice, and repeats magic values like 4rem and 34rem. Its root-font bump on very wide screens also partly undercuts the stop-growing goal. B has small lapses of its own: 52ch and 16.25rem are hard-coded rather than tokenized, and the 4/8/12 columns in its table are never implemented, but it is cleaner overall.
